definition: In mathematics, the structure tensor, also referred to as the second-moment matrix, is a matrix derived from the gradient of a function.
details: It describes the distribution of the gradient in a specified neighborhood around a point and makes the information invariant to the observing coordinates. The structure tensor is often used in image processing and computer vision.

explainer.lead: A matrix derived from the gradient of a function that describes how the gradient is distributed in a neighborhood around a point. It matters because it makes that information invariant to the observing coordinates.

tiers.eli5: At each spot in a picture, it summarizes which way the edges and shading run, so the answer stays the same no matter how you turn the page.
tiers.practitioner: Used in image processing and computer vision to summarize local gradient structure; a pitfall is that the neighborhood size must be chosen carefully, since it sets the scale of structure captured.
tiers.paperLevel: Also called the second-moment matrix; it is derived from the gradient of a function and describes the gradient's distribution in a specified neighborhood around a point, making the information invariant to observing coordinates.

explainer.example: In an image, the structure tensor at a point summarizes the gradients in the surrounding neighborhood in a coordinate-invariant form.
